name: Alphafly Next% 1
blurb: The marathon weapon. Feels like cheating right up until mile 22, when it feels like salvation.
sole: Full-length carbon plate + dual Air Zoom pods
review: Race mornings only. The Air pods feel gimmicky for about a mile, then the marathon math starts working in your favor. Legs noticeably less wrecked at the finish.

name: Adizero Adios Pro 3
blurb: Carbon rods instead of a plate. The rival race shoe that keeps the Vaporflys honest.
review: The rods feel stranger than a plate — more roll, less snap — but at threshold pace everything clicks into a rhythm the Vaporfly can't quite match.

name: FuelCell Rebel v4
blurb: The most fun per mile in the closet. Light, bouncy, and a little smug about it.
review: No plate, no rules. It begs for strides on easy days, which is a character flaw I share. Best pure fun in the rotation.

name: Blazer Mid '77
blurb: Older design than most of the closet. Still the best-looking thing on this shelf.
review: Bought for the colorway, kept for everything else. Stiff out of the box, perfect after two weeks.

name: Speedcross 6
blurb: Mud, roots, questionable shortcuts. Grips everything, apologizes for nothing.
review: Ankle-deep mud is its love language. Overkill on dry hardpack, unstoppable everywhere else.

name: Yeezy 450
blurb: Looks like nothing else on earth. Half the compliments, all the double takes.
review: Objectively ridiculous, which is the point. More comfortable than it has any right to be, and the double takes never stop.

name: Ultraboost Light
blurb: Half trainer, half errand shoe. Logs miles, then gets groceries.
review: Boost finally on a diet. Still more errand shoe than trainer, but the miles it does get are plush ones.

name: SuperComp Trainer v3
blurb: Long-run machine. Big stack, big plans, big Sunday energy.
review: The plate shows up around mile 12 and carries the back half of every long run. Big shoe, big weekend energy.

name: Vaporfly Next% 1
blurb: The original supershoe. Retired from racing, kept for the history books.
review: The shoe that started the arms race. Retired at peak, displayed like a trophy, occasionally worn to remember why.

name: ZoomX Dragonfly
blurb: Track spikes with a foam habit. Every rep feels a little bit downhill.
review: Reps feel a gear cheaper than they should. Strictly rationed to keep the magic.

name: Blazer Mid '77 Vintage
blurb: The everyday pair. Comfortable at hour ten, looks fine with everything.
review: Hour-ten comfort with a suit-or-shorts range. The default answer to "which shoes."

name: Fresh Foam X More v4
blurb: All the foam New Balance could legally sell. For the day after the long day.
review: A mattress with laces, in the best way. The day-after-the-long-day shoe that keeps the rest of the week honest.

name: Vaporfly Next% 2
blurb: Same magic, friendlier upper. The pair that made a PR feel like a formality.
review: Same engine, better cockpit. Wore them to a PR that felt suspiciously easy — still not giving the shoe all the credit, just most of it.

name: Zoom Victory XC 5
blurb: Cross country spikes. Mud, hills, elbows — these were there for all of it.
review: Mud, hills, and elbows for two seasons. Spikes chewed down to nubs and still asking for another race.

name: Arizona
blurb: The first thing on after any long run, and I will not be shamed.
review: First thing on after every long run. Cork molds to the foot; opinions mold to the cork.

name: Fresh Foam X 1080
blurb: The dependable one. Never the headline, always on the schedule.
review: Never the exciting pick, always the correct one. The schedule runs through it.

name: Vaporfly 3
blurb: Lighter, softer, somehow faster. Only comes out when there's a bib involved.
review: Lighter and softer than the 2, and somehow angrier at slow paces. Bib-number days only.

name: Air Zoom Tempo Next%
blurb: The Alphafly's practice-squad sibling. Workout days without burning race legs.
review: All the Alphafly's parts at practice-squad prices — heavier, sturdier, and happy to eat Tuesday workouts so the race pair doesn't have to.

name: Blazer Mid '77
blurb: Third Blazer, no regrets. A colorway too good to leave in the store.
review: Zero justification, no regrets. Some colorways you just don't leave in the store.

name: Zoom Fly 4 Premium
blurb: Carbon plate on a commuter's budget. Does the workhorse miles with a bit of pop.
review: The plate's there, the magic's rationed. Perfect for hard-ish days when burning the Vaporflys feels wasteful.

name: Pegasus Turbo Next Nature
blurb: Recycled ZoomX and endless steady miles. The quiet overachiever of the rotation.
review: Recycled ZoomX with none of the guilt and most of the pop. Quietly logs more miles than anything else here.

name: Pegasus 40 Duke
blurb: The workhorse in school colors. Easy days, long days, most days.
review: A Pegasus in school colors — does everything, complains never. Campus miles counted double.

name: Vaporfly 4
blurb: Still box-fresh. Currently accepting applications from goal races.
review: Still in the tissue paper. Rating is provisional until a goal race says otherwise.

name: Pegasus 38 Shield
blurb: The bad-weather clause of the rotation. Rain on the forecast, these by the door.
review: Wet-pavement traction that makes winter feel optional. The forecast picks these, not me.

name: Pegasus 37
blurb: Hundreds of miles deep and still asking for more. Retired with honors.
review: Five hundred miles of everything. Retired with full honors and a permanent spot in the hall.

name: Vomero 18
blurb: Soft, green, and entirely unbothered by pace. Easy days only.
review: Soft without being sloppy. Easy days actually stay easy, which is rarer than it sounds.

name: Vomero Plus
blurb: Maximum cushion, zero agenda. The recovery run's best argument.
review: The recovery run's best argument. All stack, no agenda, knees send thank-you notes.

name: Invincible Run
blurb: Running on marshmallows, officially licensed. Legs feel brand new the next morning.
review: Marshmallow physics. The morning-after shoe that makes yesterday's long run someone else's problem.

name: Killshot 2
blurb: The retro tennis shoe the internet made famous. Gum sole, clean lines, goes with everything.
review: The internet's favorite tennis shoe for a reason. Gum sole, clean lines, zero notes.
